text: In South Korea, the government says that having one child earns you 2 million won, which is about 40 million won in our currency.
Hungary goes even further, granting women who have four or more children a lifetime exemption from personal income tax
Japan has even established an agency dedicated to caring for children and families
Yet, in these countries, the birth rate is still declining
I was reading these statistics and wondering why people still refuse to have children even with money
The normal logic is that they're probably too poor to have children. But now that they have money, they should have more children, right? People used to have many children even when they were poor
To explain this, we have to go back to the first step of starting a family: dating. And we'll use the theoretical framework of game theory to explain why dating is becoming increasingly difficult
Why are there so many dating apps, yet people are still single
And with this trend of no one getting married or having children, many countries will disappear within 100 years

Welcome to our cat-themed adaptation series. We're adapting great foreign videos into Vietnamese for you to refer to. Actually, we've always done this, but now we're going to do it more officially. And our first series is the game theory series from the Predictive History channel
In this video, we'll base our content on those videos, as well as add our own research and counter-arguments, so we can have more productive meals, sleep, and bass washing sessions

Okay, let's begin. First, let's talk a little about game theory. Any game will have three parts: the players, which are the participants; the rules, which are the constraints, the limitations, what can and cannot be done; and the rewards
Because there must be rewards in a game; no one plays for no reason. It's what makes players want to play
To understand a game, we need to understand who is playing, what the rules are, and what the rewards are. And if we understand those three things, we can guess where the game will go.
Okay, now let's apply this theoretical framework to the dating story. Now imagine a society with 10 people, five men, five women, and all of them want to date and get married
These five men will belong to five different social classes and will be ranked from 1 to 5 based on criteria such as appearance, health, wealth, and social status
Number five will be the ultimate catch, while number one will be the lowest
Instinctively, all women will want to marry number five, and all five men will want to marry all five women at the same time
This is because women want a partner who is capable of protecting and providing for them, while men want to maximize their fertility, so they want to date many women
However, if all the women only chase after number five, it won't work
Because the other four men will team up to deal with number five
If number five decides to date all five women at the same time, then number five will realize that number five is no longer the most desirable person
Because this guy is too promiscuous and doesn't guarantee a future for himself, the best option for girl number 5 at this point would be guy number 4
At this point, girl number 4 will lose her best option, so she'll have to choose guy number 3
Then girl number 3 will have to marry guy number 2. And girl number 2 will marry guy number 1
And the result is that guy number 5, the most eager one, ends up stuck with girl number 1
Actually, girl number 3 could still marry guy number 5 because the difference between 5 and 2 is quite large. But to simplify, let's just assume the above

And the final result is that guy number 5, who should have gotten the best result, gets the worst result. All the girls get worse results than they should have, except for girl number 1. The only good thing is that all the guys benefit
Actually, this is just a small assumption to illustrate the point: in a game, the strongest person who is too greedy will suffer a bitter end, and their rivals will be the ones who benefit directly
From this, we can deduce that the strongest person isn't the one who can steal everything from everyone else, but the one who can coordinate so that everyone benefits the most
Because if they just steal, the strongest person might win in the short term, but in the long term, everyone will lose
Because even though Mr. Four gets Ms. Five, there's still a disparity between the two, so conflicts and difficulties will inevitably arise
Therefore, the best solution is cooperation. Mr. Five takes Ms. Five, Mr. Four takes Ms. Four, Mr. Three takes Ms. Three – everyone finds a partner, everyone has children, and society develops

This state — game theory calls it Nash equilibrium. This is a state where no one benefits more from unilaterally changing strategies. It's like everyone is happy, and any change would only lead to more losses.
So, let's just keep things as they are. Okay. That theory is perfectly fine. But there's a problem: society doesn't just have 10 people, but 8 billion people. So, there's...

A fun survey asks: If you're 30 years old, your parents are pressuring you to get married, you've been dating for 10 years and haven't found anyone you like, and now you're forced to get married, what are your minimum requirements for agreeing to marry someone

I think it would be simpler for guys. Like, any girl will do, even girl number one would be fine. Some girls say that if I don't love that guy now, if I don't find him attractive, then at least he must be earning around 200 million a month
According to Nash equilibrium, number three should marry number three and live happily. But in reality, number three will look at number three and think, "It's better to stay single

Unless I meet number five or he earns 200 million a month, then I won't consider it. Because there's no reason to suffer by getting involved with someone who's on par with me, risking having to be on par with him and then having to cater to him

In reality, many people rush into the top 1-2%, and most end up being left behind. For example, Elon Musk, he has a ton of children and many wives. Billionaires and celebrities have no shortage of people lining up for them
Meanwhile, many young people around the world are also experiencing the situation of being involuntarily single. That is, they want a partner, they want to get married, but they can't

So gradually, they give up. As for the guys, they'd rather stay home playing games, browsing the internet, and watching movies. So, many young men in their 25s and 30s have never dated, never had a relationship, and don't want to try anymore

Grandpa, that sounds like me, right? It's not because they're ugly or incompetent, but simply because the dating game now is too tiring. The competition is fierce, and the probability of winning is low

That's the theory that says balancing things out is the optimal approach. But in reality, people don't want to play that game anymore. Why? As I said, in a game there are three parts: the players. This hasn't changed much. The rules of the game are competition, and that hasn't changed much.

The final thing is the reward. It seems that the rewards of dating in modern times have changed somewhat. Usually, we think of dating rewards as love, sex, marriage, and having children. But now there's another very important element
It was important in the past, but now it's exaggerated a lot. It's social status, meaning your reputation and your position in the eyes of others
Simply put, if you love this person and marry this person, can you show them off

Can you be proud in the eyes of others? Can you show them off on Facebook? Can you show them off on Instagram? Can you show them off at a class reunion and brag about how handsome and rich your husband is, or how hot and capable your wife is? Now, the story has added an extremely important element: reputation

And it doesn't just stop at marriage. It also manifests in things like the latest iPhone, luxurious travel and check-ins, and buying designer goods. Many people do things not because they actually use them, but because they want to show off
And marriage is also part of this game. If you marry someone who isn't worthy, it will be embarrassing. So it's better to be single than to marry someone who doesn't meet the standards.

The scary thing is that the game of showing off is a zero-sum game. That means there will always be people better and people worse off. If everyone could show off, then no one would be able to show off
Because if everyone showed off, then no one would be. If there are people at the top, there must be people at the bottom
There are many opinions that the government of various countries giving money to people to encourage having children is ineffective. Because the problem isn't a lack of money

Nowadays, finding a job is easier. I know there's a lot of unemployment now, but it's easier than in the past. In the past, people only knew how to work in the fields. Now there are more choices. So now, people can find a normal job, be healthy, and at least earn enough to live on
But the important thing is that people lack face. And face can't necessarily be bought with money
If you give people 1 billion to force them to marry someone their friends look down on, what meaning does that 1 billion have? Actually, it does have meaning, but in the end
In those cases, some people would rather not marry a billion dollars than have to get married
Here's a question: why do humans always chase after this kind of "face" while our species has survived for tens of thousands of years, remaining very numerous and not becoming extinct? The answer is:

From Mr. Giang in the Preditive History channel, it's that humans didn't behave like that before because the game has changed over time. Game theory has a concept called the overall picture of society, that is, the big context surrounding the game

Specifically in this case, it's the population size, whether society is rich or poor, whether there are external enemies, how advanced the technology is. These factors combine to determine which game is played. When the context changes, the game changes too
Now, let's divide human history into three stages for easier understanding

The first stage is the primitive era. A small village at that time had only about 200 people. Everything was inconvenient and scarce. People had to defecate in the fields, sometimes even getting bitten by snakes. And to get clean water, they had to carry it home and boil it before drinking
Having children in such circumstances was like stepping into a death trap

In that context, there was no concept of love or dating; women and men would have many lovers at the same time, firstly to increase the chances of reproduction for everyone, and secondly to avoid knowing whose child was whose
When the men in the village all thought the child might be theirs, everyone would flock together to protect and care for it. And the reward would be ensuring the entire village didn't become extinct

Let's move on to the second stage, when the small village started to expand into a society of tens of thousands of people. At this point, there was money coming in and going out, and some rudimentary technology
At this time, villages, communes, and tribes began fighting each other incessantly to compete for territory and resources. Therefore, society became extremely short of people
Because there was a need for soldiers to go to war, and people to work in the fields. In such a chaotic situation, where would they find the time for courtship and romantic dates

And so, arranged marriages took center stage. Parents decided where their children were, with no room for argument. At this point, whether the child was born or not, whether they liked it or not, didn't matter, as long as they got married and had many children
And finally, the third stage is the present day. Now the world is crowded, with 8 billion people. Look at China or India, each country has over 1 billion people, very crowded
And there's much more money too. But some people have more than enough while others struggle to make ends meet, which is very unequal
The upside is that healthcare is better, technology is more advanced, so women who give birth are almost guaranteed to survive, reducing the risk of childbirth being a death sentence
And then, the world is relatively peaceful in a certain way. The superpowers no longer directly shoot each other with guns, but instead wage proxy wars
Or, if they just talk big, life would be much better. But because life is better, people expect dating to be good too
While dating, falling in love, and marriage, like everything else, must have both good and bad aspects

So if you have to endure hardship, why date someone from the same social class and suffer together? Why not choose someone from a higher social class? So now, dating is pretty much like a jump-starting platform
Low-level clouds try to climb to higher levels. Apps like Tinder, Bumble, or Facebook Ding are essentially platforms where people try to find a better match to jump to
But the problem is, if everyone wants to jump to a higher level, who will want to marry someone at their own level
It's like, being at level three but wanting to be at level five, or at most level four, because if you say you're at level three like yourself, then just stay put
So, marriage and childbirth are plummeting. And Mr. Giang says that if this trend continues, society will collapse sooner or later
And according to him, history has already proven it. The clearest sign of a collapsing civilization is when women with money and education start refusing to have children
He says, "Really? I don't know about that." Don't say I'm looking down on women. I love women very much
Although, in part, the Roman Empire, when it collapsed, faced the same scenario. Those who valued...

the Romans at that time were both rich and skilled, so they decided not to have children or to have very few. And the situation became so serious that Emperor Augustus had to enact the Lexuria law to punish those who were lazy to marry and reward those who had many children
That means more than 2000 years ago, people tried using money and policies to solve the problem. But the results were not very effective
Rome still collapsed as usual, though. I think it wasn't just because of the lack of births that Rome collapsed, but there were many other reasons as well. This is just one part of the story

Speaking of collapse, let's look at the numbers. Currently, the replacement birth rate is 2.1 children per woman. That means a mother has to give birth to at least two children for the population to remain at its current level
Below 2.1, we start seeing a shortage of people. Below 1.5, the decline is rapid. If it drops below 1.0, then society is essentially self-destructing
Looking at the world map, we see it's divided into two states: in Africa, people still have very high birth rates. In some regions, each mother gives birth to five to seven children
Because there, they are still in the stage where they need people to survive and then fight for territory and things like that, so they just have as many children as possible to compensate

Meanwhile, in the wealthy regions of North America, Europe, and East Asia, the birth rate is plummeting. In North America and Europe, there are still immigrants; if native women don't want to have children, then so be it
They will open their doors to foreigners to work, pay taxes, and contribute to the economy. But it also causes a lot of headaches in terms of culture and politics
We just need to read international news to see it. Immigration is always the hottest issue, with heated arguments in Europe and America. And in East Asia, we're really sitting on a powder keg.

Because here, there's no such thing as easily opening the doors to immigrants. Because East Asian culture is quite closed, it's very difficult to accept complete strangers and have them sit at the same table
South Korea is a prime example; their birth rate has now dropped to around 0.6 to 0.8, the lowest in the world
With this population, South Korea will probably only survive for a few more generations before disappearing from the map

Now, there are even restaurants there with signs saying "no kids allowed," a so-called "no kid zone." It's as if they consider children to be a nuisance, noisy, and ruining the experience for other customers
According to Mr. Giang, South Korea is like that because it's a society that values ​​appearances to an extreme degree. Everything has to be beautiful, high-quality, and expensive

The proof is in the Korean showbiz industry, from idols to actors; everyone has to be perfectly beautiful. But where do idols and shows come from? And usually, people in Korea are also caught up in this "perfection trap
And because of that, the path to success there is quite narrow. Either you get into a prestigious university and work for Samsung or some other big corporation, or you have no decent options at all
So, if you're a middle-class family in Korea, you'll hear this economic argument: If you have three children, you need more than three times the money and resources

If none of them can afford to get into a top university, then just pour everything into one child and send them to extra classes from early morning until late at night. Hopefully, they'll pass and change their lives
And this logic forces people to only dare to have one child, or to just stop having children altogether to avoid the burden
Currently, the Korean population seems relatively stable because there's still a fairly large working-age population, but by around 2040, the imbalance will start
The elderly population will skyrocket while the number of children will dwindle. By 2060, the workforce will be halved

At that point, no one will work, and no one will serve in the military. So, a society where everyone is just old folks sitting around in parks with no one creating wealth will only lead to a national economic collapse
China is the same. Now the birth rate is only about 1.0.
whereas five years ago it was still 1.7, but now it's plummeting. At this rate, by the end of the century, China's population will probably only be half
That's around 600 million. Actually, it's still a lot, but with so many elderly people, they won't be able to support such a huge system

Speaking of birth rates, there's a rather interesting comparison: usually, the richer a country is, the fewer children it has. But there are exceptions; this country is also rich and has very advanced technology, yet each family still has more than two children
So, if we explain it using game theory, the reward in Israel is different because of its history and religion
Having children is linked to community consciousness and national identity. That is, having children is seen as a way to enhance one's prestige, something to be proud of, not a burden
Or in the oil-rich country, people still have many children because they have oil, and the state provides everything from A to Z – healthcare, housing, everything is free
Plus, religious factors encourage having many children, so people just keep having them. You might ask if this model will survive if the oil runs out in the future. Only the future will tell
The key point here is that, from a game theory perspective, societies that consider having children as a way to enhance prestige will have high birth rates

Conversely, societies that consider having children as a way to diminish prestige, like... If having children means losing freedom, money, time, and opportunities for advancement, then people will choose not to have children
So now the question is, what about Vietnam?
In 2024, our birth rate will fall to 1.91 per woman, the lowest in history. This is the third consecutive year we've been below 2.1. The downward trend is very clear
We lose a little each year, but it's worth noting that 2024 is the Year of the Dragon, and according to our culture, the Year of the Dragon is a very auspicious year to have children
The person writing this script is also born in the Year of the Dragon. But even with such strong spiritual beliefs, they can't win against the game of saving face in modern society
Everyone knows that the Year of the Dragon is auspicious, but thinking about the expense and fatigue of raising children and how it will affect their careers, people just give up on having children

In those big cities, the birth rate is only 1.67. In rural areas, it's slightly higher, but it's also declining. Ho Chi Minh City, however, has the lowest rate in the country at only 1.39, while the age of first marriage continues to rise

Men now have to be around 30 to get married, and women around 25. This aligns quite well with the theoretical framework of the game: the more educated and wealthier people are, the fewer children they have because they have too much to lose when it comes to having children

Many experts predict that if this continues, after 2035, Vietnam's population will start experiencing negative growth. That is, the number of deaths will exceed the number of births. Seven provinces seem to have already begun experiencing this situation
Although Vietnam isn't as dire as South Korea or China, we are still on the same path. And we are also heavily influenced by social media

In the old days, people lived in a small village or neighborhood of only a few hundred people. They only compared themselves to the people around them. The probability of becoming the top person in the neighborhood was quite high.
Even if they went to Hanoi or Saigon, they were actually only average, so they were still happy to get married so their children could live happily, with less comparison. They were considered great

Now it's completely different. On TikTok, you see guys with six-pack abs driving Porsches or those making a fortune in business. On Instagram, you see girls with white skin and slim waists carrying handbags and eating omochi
Anyone successful is known to the whole society. So, naturally, you start comparing yourself to millions of people online
And then, the people around you don't seem good enough anymore. Social media expanded the playing field from 200-300 people to millions, pushing the standards up unreasonably
Dating apps are the same; swiping back and forth through hundreds of people every day tricks your brain into thinking you have too many choices

There's no need to rush. Just keep swiping a little longer, you'll start meeting better people, and the result is that you end up not choosing anyone, or you might not like them even if you do go on a date
From a game theory perspective, social media has increased the number of players a thousandfold while the number of prizes at the top remains the same, the winning rate is practically zero
But people still play because they see everyone else playing
Actually, after watching the video and writing the script, we realized that this game theory doesn't help us answer the question immediately; it only helps us know how to ask the right question
Naturally, for any situation, you should ask yourself who the players are, what the rules are, and what the rewards are
From there, you can see the overall picture to see where society is and where it's going. Dating is just one example
We can apply this to everything, from the tense situation between the US and Iran to the war in Ukraine, or why this is an opportunity for Vietnam to break through
